records.originalText: Don't risk your neck over something foolish.
records.finalText: Don't risk your neck over something foolish.
records.rationale: The figurative risk-your-neck warning is idiomatic and its foolish action is adequately bounded.

records.originalText: I caught sight of a fly escaping from the room.
records.finalText: I caught sight of a fly escaping from the room.
records.rationale: Caught sight of naturally introduces a brief observation; the escaping fly supplies a complete event.

records.originalText: I can't find my pipe.
records.finalText: I can't find my pipe.
records.rationale: Pragmatic repeat of the existing missing-gloves example; substituting pipe does not add a new proposition.

records.originalText: She got a run in her stocking when she broke the heel of her shoe.
records.finalText: She got a run in her stocking when she broke the heel of her shoe.
records.rationale: Run in her stocking is a valid American expression; the when clause locates the mishap.

records.originalText: Would you like another helping of pie?
records.finalText: Would you like another helping of pie?
records.rationale: Another helping of pie is a natural polite offer using a food quantity expression.

records.originalText: I got a motorbike cheap.
records.finalText: I got a motorbike cheap.
records.rationale: Cheap functions idiomatically as an informal adverb after the purchase construction.

records.originalText: Here is your appointment card.
records.finalText: Here is your appointment card.
records.rationale: A conventional appointment-card handover is complete as direct speech.

records.originalText: The party was a marked success.
records.finalText: The party was a marked success.
records.rationale: Marked success is a natural evaluative collocation about a particular party.

records.originalText: The party was, on the whole, successful.
records.finalText: The party was, on the whole, successful.
records.rationale: Repeats the party-success proposition retained in 35621; on the whole adds little learning content.

records.originalText: I feel in my bones that the party will be a great success.
records.finalText: I feel in my bones that the party will be a great success.
records.rationale: Feel in my bones is an idiomatic prediction, distinct from the completed party assessment.

records.originalText: The party broke up late.
records.finalText: The party broke up late.
records.rationale: Broke up expresses the party ending and late supplies an adequate time complement.

records.originalText: My brother saw to all the arrangements for the party.
records.finalText: My brother saw to all the arrangements for the party.
records.rationale: Saw to all the arrangements idiomatically describes taking responsibility for a specific party.

records.originalText: I've mistakenly deleted the party information and registration you sent to me.
records.finalText: I've mistakenly deleted the party information and registration you sent to me.
records.rationale: The present-perfect deletion report and relative clause form a complete digital mishap.

records.originalText: Her behavior at the party was far from perfect.
records.finalText: Her behavior at the party was far from perfect.
records.rationale: Far from perfect expresses a specific speaker evaluation, without a universal behavior claim.

records.originalText: Blow out all the candles on the birthday cake at once.
records.finalText: Blow out all the candles on the birthday cake at once.
records.rationale: The birthday-candle imperative is natural and presents an ordinary celebration activity.

records.originalText: The situation has come to the point where we either sink or swim.
records.finalText: The situation has come to the point where we either sink or swim.
records.rationale: Sink or swim is a coherent figurative alternative in a complete situation statement.

records.originalText: Words of abuse poured from his lips.
records.finalText: Words of abuse poured from his lips.
records.rationale: Words of abuse poured from his lips is literary but grammatical reported behavior.

records.originalText: My throat feels clogged up.
records.finalText: My throat feels clogged up.
records.rationale: Clogged up conveys a speaker's throat sensation without offering medical diagnosis or advice.

records.originalText: The Nozomi is the fastest of all the trains in Japan.
records.finalText: The Nozomi is the fastest of all the trains in Japan.
records.rationale: The unqualified present-day fastest-train superlative needs historical and service-category verification.

records.originalText: Irene Pepperberg, a researcher at Northwestern University, is discovering that a parrot can not only mimic people but also learn the meaning of words.
records.finalText: Irene Pepperberg, a researcher at Northwestern University, is discovering that a parrot can not only mimic people but also learn the meaning of words.
records.rationale: The present institutional affiliation and research-status claim is time-dependent and not verified by this pin.

records.originalText: Hey, come on. Don't make a face.
records.finalText: Hey, come on. Don't make a face.
records.rationale: The two imperatives form natural informal direct speech about a facial reaction.

records.originalText: A mouse is a timid creature.
records.finalText: A mouse is a timid creature.
records.rationale: The generic claim portrays all mice as timid; retain situated animal observations instead.

records.originalText: The rat made a hole in the wall.
records.finalText: The rat made a hole in the wall.
records.rationale: A specific rat making a hole is a grammatical, self-contained past event.

records.originalText: A bat is no more a bird than a rat is.
records.finalText: A bat is no more a bird than a rat is.
records.rationale: No more a bird than compares two non-birds coherently and illustrates a less common comparison frame.

records.originalText: Rats have gnawed holes in the door.
records.finalText: Rats have gnawed holes in the door.
records.rationale: Gnawed holes is a natural resultative collocation with an observable present-perfect result.

records.originalText: The screw, the lever, the wedge, the pulley, etc. are called simple machines.
records.finalText: The screw, the lever, the wedge, the pulley, etc. are called simple machines.
records.rationale: The open-ended etc. list is an incomplete instructional definition requiring technical scope review.

records.originalText: Clerks with sticky fingers won't keep their jobs for long.
records.finalText: Clerks with sticky fingers won't keep their jobs for long.
records.rationale: The prediction about all dishonest clerks' job retention is an unsupported universal causal claim.

records.originalText: Cats were domesticated by the Egyptians.
records.finalText: Cats were domesticated by the Egyptians.
records.rationale: The exclusive-looking historical domestication statement oversimplifies a complex origin claim.

records.originalText: The cat's fur stood on end.
records.finalText: The cat's fur stood on end.
records.rationale: Fur stood on end is a natural description of one cat's physical reaction.

records.originalText: A cat got out from under the car.
records.finalText: A cat got out from under the car.
records.rationale: Got out from under the car supplies both movement and a clear spatial origin.

records.originalText: Hold still a moment while I fix your tie.
records.finalText: Hold still a moment while I fix your tie.
records.rationale: Hold still and fix your tie form a natural, complete request during a clothing adjustment.

records.originalText: I left some scallions out on the veranda for too long and they dried out.
records.finalText: I left some scallions out on the veranda for too long and they dried out.
records.rationale: The scallions and veranda vocabulary adds difficulty; the drying event is coherent and bounded.

records.originalText: Honey, will you go shopping for me?
records.finalText: Honey, will you go shopping for me?
records.rationale: The affectionate address and shopping request are ordinary self-contained direct speech.

records.originalText: My, you're looking green around the gills.
records.finalText: My, you're looking green around the gills.
records.rationale: Green around the gills is a conventional idiom for appearance, with no medical advice implied.

records.originalText: The wet vase left a mark on the table.
records.finalText: The wet vase left a mark on the table.
records.rationale: The wet vase leaving a mark describes a concrete past result naturally.

records.originalText: Clean the window with a damp cloth.
records.finalText: Clean the window with a damp cloth.
records.rationale: A damp cloth is a natural cleaning collocation in an ordinary household instruction.

records.originalText: Garlic enhances the flavor of meals.
records.finalText: Garlic enhances the flavor of meals.
records.rationale: The culinary flavor statement is conventional and modest, with no health or universal-effect claim.

records.originalText: Carrots and turnips are edible roots.
records.finalText: Carrots and turnips are edible roots.
records.rationale: The elementary edible-root classification is stable and grammatically clear.

records.originalText: We were caught in a shower and got wet to the skin.
records.finalText: We were caught in a shower and got wet to the skin.
records.rationale: Repeats the published caught-in-a-shower and wet-to-the-skin incident; removing the journey frame adds no distinct content.

records.originalText: How many flights to New York do you offer a week?
records.finalText: How many flights to New York do you offer a week?
records.rationale: The weekly-flight question is complete and illustrates a normal travel enquiry.

records.originalText: How many flights to New York do you offer a day?
records.finalText: How many flights to New York do you offer a day?
records.rationale: The daily-flight question repeats 35881 with only the frequency unit changed.

records.originalText: If you visit New York, you've just got to come and see our house.
records.finalText: If you visit New York, you've just got to come and see our house.
records.rationale: The visit invitation uses natural emphatic have got to within a conditional frame.

records.originalText: His business in New York was a great success.
records.finalText: His business in New York was a great success.
records.rationale: A particular person's successful New York business is a coherent past evaluation.

records.originalText: The ship from New York will arrive before long.
records.finalText: The ship from New York will arrive before long.
records.rationale: Before long is a natural arrival-time expression about a specific ship.

records.originalText: Newton established the law of gravity.
records.finalText: Newton established the law of gravity.
records.rationale: The conventional historical attribution concerns Newton's gravity law, without a changing current claim.

records.originalText: It occurred to me that I should keep the news to myself.
records.finalText: It occurred to me that I should keep the news to myself.
records.rationale: It occurred to me and keep the news to myself form a coherent private realization.

records.originalText: What's New Zealand like? Is it as sparsely populated as Australia?
records.finalText: What's New Zealand like? Is it as sparsely populated as Australia?
records.rationale: Sparsely populated adds lexical difficulty; the comparative is framed as a question rather than an asserted statistic.

records.originalText: Nickel is a hard, silver-white metal.
records.finalText: Nickel is a hard, silver-white metal.
records.rationale: The basic metal description is stable and silver-white is an intelligible color compound.

records.originalText: Nixon was caught lying because he bugged his own office.
records.finalText: Nixon was caught lying because he bugged his own office.
records.rationale: The Watergate causal explanation is compressed and historically misleading without source verification.

records.originalText: Nikita Khrushchev was at the height of his powers.
records.finalText: Nikita Khrushchev was at the height of his powers.
records.rationale: At the height of his powers lacks a period or event for a standalone historical assessment.

records.originalText: Not knowing what to answer, I kept silent.
records.finalText: Not knowing what to answer, I kept silent.
records.rationale: The participial reason clause and main past clause agree naturally in subject and time.

records.originalText: What a big dog that is!
records.finalText: What a big dog that is!
records.rationale: The dog exclamation is grammatical and complete with a clear demonstrative referent in direct speech.

records.originalText: Not knowing what to say, I kept silent.
records.finalText: Not knowing what to say, I kept silent.
records.rationale: Near paraphrase of 36008: not knowing an answer or what to say leads to the same silence.

records.originalText: What a wonderful morning! I feel on top of the world.
records.finalText: What a wonderful morning! I feel on top of the world.
records.rationale: The paired exclamation and on-top-of-the-world idiom form coherent positive direct speech.

records.originalText: I managed to get out of the crowd.
records.finalText: I managed to get out of the crowd.
records.rationale: Managed to get out expresses successful movement from a specified crowd.

records.originalText: You must try and come to the party.
records.finalText: You must try and come to the party.
records.rationale: Repeats the published invitation hoping the listener can come to the party, with only stronger insistence.

records.originalText: You had better apologize to him for that failure in some way or other.
records.finalText: You had better apologize to him for that failure in some way or other.
records.rationale: Had better and in some way or other form a complete, if formal, apology recommendation.

records.originalText: I will finish this work somehow.
records.finalText: I will finish this work somehow.
records.rationale: The future promise with somehow is a natural expression of determination.

records.originalText: What a hot day it is!
records.finalText: What a hot day it is!
records.rationale: What a hot day is a complete everyday weather exclamation.

records.originalText: What a gorgeous coat you're wearing!
records.finalText: What a gorgeous coat you're wearing!
records.rationale: Gorgeous coat supplies a specific clothing compliment in a natural exclamative clause.

records.originalText: What a stroke of luck!
records.finalText: What a stroke of luck!
records.rationale: Stroke of luck is a conventional complete exclamation with useful idiomatic vocabulary.

records.originalText: What are you making all the fuss about?
records.finalText: What are you making all the fuss about?
records.rationale: Make a fuss about is an idiomatic question about a reaction, grammatically complete.

records.originalText: What a lovely day it is!
records.finalText: What a lovely day it is!
records.rationale: Another short day-evaluation exclamation adds little beyond 36030 and 36080.

records.originalText: Oh, no! My house is on fire!
records.finalText: Oh, no! My house is on fire!
records.rationale: The alarm and house-on-fire statement are complete emergency direct speech without harmful instructions.

records.originalText: Looks like I might have to burn the midnight oil tonight.
records.finalText: Looks like I might have to burn the midnight oil tonight.
records.rationale: Looks like is valid informal subject ellipsis; burn the midnight oil describes anticipated late work.

records.originalText: I'm kind of sick today.
records.finalText: I'm kind of sick today.
records.rationale: Kind of is a natural informal degree modifier in a speaker's present health report.

records.originalText: I envy your lifestyle - living day-to-day like that.
records.finalText: I envy your lifestyle - living day-to-day like that.
records.rationale: The envy statement and explanatory supplement form coherent personal direct speech.

records.originalText: It is true that he is poor, but he is contented.
records.finalText: It is true that he is poor, but he is contented.
records.rationale: Contented is valid adjective use and the concession concerns one individual, not a group stereotype.

records.originalText: He may be clever, but he is not very helpful.
records.finalText: He may be clever, but he is not very helpful.
records.rationale: May be clever contrasts ability and helpfulness naturally in a specific personal assessment.

records.originalText: It may, indeed, be a mistake.
records.finalText: It may, indeed, be a mistake.
records.rationale: It may be a mistake has no content anchor and merely contributes a discourse hedge.

records.originalText: Well, you may be right.
records.finalText: Well, you may be right.
records.rationale: A generic agreement response has too little independent learning content for this example lane.

records.originalText: I'd like to come to see the doctor as soon as possible.
records.finalText: I'd like to come to see the doctor as soon as possible.
records.rationale: The doctor-appointment request is polite, complete and free of clinical advice.

records.originalText: Could you speak as slowly as possible?
records.finalText: Could you speak as slowly as possible?
records.rationale: Pragmatic repeat of the published request to speak more slowly; as possible adds only emphasis.

records.originalText: Do you think I was born yesterday?
records.finalText: Do you think I was born yesterday?
records.rationale: Born yesterday is a conventional idiomatic rhetorical question about gullibility.

records.originalText: Napoleon was exiled to St. Helena.
records.finalText: Napoleon was exiled to St. Helena.
records.rationale: The passive exile statement is a stable historical event with an explicit destination.

records.originalText: Napoleon called the English a nation of shopkeepers.
records.finalText: Napoleon called the English a nation of shopkeepers.
records.rationale: The attributed national quotation needs quotation provenance and framing beyond a source sentence.

records.originalText: Had Napoleon been born in this century, what could he have done?
records.finalText: Had Napoleon been born in this century, what could he have done?
records.rationale: This century has no anchored date and makes the historical counterfactual unstable as a standalone example.

records.originalText: Naples is a picturesque city.
records.finalText: Naples is a picturesque city.
records.rationale: Picturesque is a subjective descriptive adjective applied to a named city.

records.originalText: Nothing will make up for his past mistakes.
records.finalText: Nothing will make up for his past mistakes.
records.rationale: Make up for naturally describes compensation for specific past mistakes.

records.originalText: Living as I do in a remote village, I seldom have visitors.
records.finalText: Living as I do in a remote village, I seldom have visitors.
records.rationale: Living as I do is a grammatical concessive-style explanatory construction with a complete main clause.

records.originalText: Give me something nice to drink.
records.finalText: Give me something nice to drink.
records.rationale: Something nice to drink is a natural indefinite-pronoun phrase in direct speech.

records.originalText: Why have the apes evolved more than other animals?
records.finalText: Why have the apes evolved more than other animals?
records.rationale: The question presupposes a false evolutionary ladder in which apes evolved more than other animals.

records.originalText: Why do we have dreams?
records.finalText: Why do we have dreams?
records.rationale: The open question about dreams makes no unsupported causal assertion.

records.originalText: What turned her against you?
records.finalText: What turned her against you?
records.rationale: Turned her against is an idiomatic causative question about a changed relationship.

records.originalText: Why are you so bitter against her?
records.finalText: Why are you so bitter toward her?
records.rationale: Bitter against is less natural here; change the preposition to toward while retaining the relationship question.

records.originalText: Would you tell me why you have refused their offer?
records.finalText: Would you tell me why you have refused their offer?
records.rationale: The polite indirect question uses correct embedded clause order and present-perfect refusal.

records.originalText: Why does he always run his son down?
records.finalText: Why does he always run his son down?
records.rationale: Run his son down is a grammatical phrasal-verb question about habitual criticism.

records.originalText: Why do you dislike his way of speaking?
records.finalText: Why do you dislike his way of speaking?
records.rationale: His way of speaking is a natural complement to dislike in a complete why question.

records.originalText: Why he got angry is quite clear.
records.finalText: Why he got angry is quite clear.
records.rationale: The embedded interrogative functions naturally as the subject of is quite clear.

records.originalText: I understand now why he didn't go to a university.
records.finalText: I understand now why he didn't go to a university.
records.rationale: The explanation of understanding and past university attendance forms a complete thought.

records.originalText: Why he killed himself is still a mystery.
records.finalText: Why he killed himself is still a mystery.
records.rationale: The unexplained suicide mystery is unsuitable as an unframed general typing example.

records.originalText: Nobody knows why he turns down my help.
records.finalText: Nobody knows why he turns down my help.
records.rationale: Turns down my help is a natural phrasal-verb complement inside an indirect question.

records.originalText: Why do I even care?
records.finalText: Why do I even care?
records.rationale: Even naturally conveys frustration in this short, complete introspective question.

records.originalText: Why don't you put your best foot forward?
records.finalText: Why don't you put your best foot forward?
records.rationale: Put your best foot forward is a conventional idiomatic suggestion in question form.

records.originalText: Why did you put off the printing of my book?
records.finalText: Why did you put off the printing of my book?
records.rationale: Put off the printing uses a nominal complement naturally in a concrete publishing question.

records.originalText: The reason why we cannot support his view will be given below.
records.finalText: The reason why we cannot support his view will be given below.
records.rationale: Will be given below depends on absent document material and does not stand alone.

records.originalText: Why do you think that way?
records.finalText: Why do you think that way?
records.rationale: Same reasoning question as the published what-is-it-that-makes-you-think-that-way example.

records.originalText: What has brought you here so early?
records.finalText: What has brought you here so early?
records.rationale: Same early-arrival motivation question as the published what-did-you-come-here-so-early-for example.

records.originalText: Why do I feel this way?
records.finalText: Why do I feel this way?
records.rationale: The introspective feel question is complete and distinct from the question about reasoning.

records.originalText: Why do you like coffee strong?
records.finalText: Why do you like coffee strong?
records.rationale: Object-complement strong naturally describes the preferred state of coffee.

records.originalText: Why did you get so angry at his mistake?
records.finalText: Why did you get so angry at his mistake?
records.rationale: The past question supplies a clear trigger for the person's anger.

records.originalText: Why do you study so hard?
records.finalText: Why do you study so hard?
records.rationale: The present why question about study effort is natural and independent.

records.originalText: Science begins when you ask why and how.
records.finalText: Science begins when you ask why and how.
records.rationale: The sweeping definition of when science begins is an aphoristic claim rather than a bounded example.

records.originalText: Why are your eyes so big?
records.finalText: Why are your eyes so big?
records.rationale: A simple present question about visible eye size is complete direct speech.

records.originalText: A promise made is a debt unpaid.
records.finalText: A promise made is a debt unpaid.
records.rationale: The unattributed proverb equating promises and debt needs proverbial framing and source context.

records.originalText: Bright ideas never occur to me.
records.finalText: Bright ideas never occur to me.
records.rationale: Occur to me is a natural cognitive expression in a personal habitual statement.

records.originalText: The Nile is the longest river in the world.
records.finalText: The Nile is the longest river in the world.
records.rationale: The longest-river ranking depends on measurement conventions and requires verification beyond this source.

records.originalText: Will you lend me your knife?
records.finalText: Will you lend me your knife?
records.rationale: The lend-me request is grammatical and does not specify harmful use of the knife.

records.originalText: Put the knives and forks back in the cupboard.
records.finalText: Put the knives and forks back in the cupboard.
records.rationale: The household storage instruction uses ordinary count nouns and a clear destination.

records.originalText: It is bad manners to eat with a knife.
records.finalText: It is bad manners to eat with a knife.
records.rationale: The unqualified manners rule is culturally dependent and should not be taught as universal.

records.originalText: Even the greatest scholar can't solve that.
records.finalText: Even the greatest scholar can't solve that.
records.rationale: That has no task referent; even the greatest scholar is unsupported hyperbole without context.

records.originalText: Every man has his price.
records.finalText: Every man has his price.
records.rationale: The universal claim that everyone can be bought is an unframed cynical maxim.

records.originalText: Please inform me of any changes in the situation.
records.finalText: Please inform me of any changes in the situation.
records.rationale: Inform me of any changes is a natural formal request with a clear situational complement.

records.originalText: What places do you enjoy?
records.finalText: What places do you enjoy?
records.rationale: Enjoy applied to places is underspecified here; visits or activities are needed for a useful standalone question.

records.originalText: What sort of coats are in fashion this year?
records.finalText: What sort of coats are in fashion this year?
records.rationale: The fashion question explicitly asks rather than asserting a changing current trend.

records.originalText: What kind of treatment will I get?
records.finalText: What kind of treatment will I get?
records.rationale: The treatment question is grammatical and makes no promise or clinical recommendation.

records.originalText: Under no circumstances should you repeat this to anyone.
records.finalText: Under no circumstances should you repeat this to anyone.
records.rationale: Under no circumstances correctly triggers inversion in a complete confidentiality instruction.

records.originalText: Why do you need change?
records.finalText: Why do you need change?
records.rationale: Change can naturally mean coins in this short enquiry without an unsupported assertion.

records.originalText: Why do you need quarters?
records.finalText: Why do you need quarters?
records.rationale: The quarters variant repeats 36630's request to explain a need for coinage.

records.originalText: No words can relieve her deep sorrow.
records.finalText: No words can relieve her deep sorrow.
records.rationale: Relieve her deep sorrow is a natural expression of personal grief rather than clinical guidance.

records.originalText: He was determined to finish the work at any cost.
records.finalText: He was determined to finish the work at any cost.
records.rationale: At any cost naturally modifies determination about a specific work task.

records.originalText: What kind of movie is it? Is it popular?
records.finalText: What kind of movie is it? Is it popular?
records.rationale: The two movie questions are grammatically complete and fit ordinary conversational direct speech.

records.originalText: How did such a strange thing come about?
records.finalText: How did such a strange thing come about?
records.rationale: Come about is a natural phrasal verb asking how an unusual event occurred.

records.originalText: Despite all my efforts, I will not have the report ready by Friday.
records.finalText: Despite all my efforts, I will not have the report ready by Friday.
records.rationale: Despite all my efforts and the future result form a coherent deadline statement.

records.originalText: No matter how fast you ran, you cannot win.
records.finalText: No matter how fast you ran, you could not win.
records.rationale: Align the modal with the past running event; this fixes tense inconsistency without changing the losing outcome.

records.originalText: No matter how humble it is, there's no place like home.
records.finalText: No matter how humble it is, there's no place like home.
records.rationale: The concessive clause and conventional home expression are coherent as a subjective sentiment.

records.originalText: No matter how rich a man is, he cannot buy love.
records.finalText: No matter how rich a man is, he cannot buy love.
records.rationale: The categorical money-cannot-buy-love maxim is an unframed generalization rather than a situated example.

records.originalText: I have to attain my purpose at all costs.
records.finalText: I have to achieve my goal at all costs.
records.rationale: Attain my purpose is overly stilted here; achieve my goal preserves the determined intention naturally.

records.originalText: No matter how hard you try, you can't finish it in a day.
records.finalText: No matter how hard you try, you can't finish it in a day.
records.rationale: No matter how hard introduces a natural concessive clause about a specific task and deadline.

records.originalText: However hard you try, you can't finish it in a day.
records.finalText: However hard you try, you can't finish it in a day.
records.rationale: Repeats 36751's same impossibility claim using however instead of no matter how.

records.originalText: However hard you try, you can't finish it in a week or so.
records.finalText: However hard you try, you can't finish it in a week or so.
records.rationale: Repeats the hard-trying deadline proposition in 36751 with only the time period changed.

records.originalText: No matter how he tried, he could not open the door.
records.finalText: No matter how he tried, he could not open the door.
records.rationale: The past concessive and failed door-opening event are coherent and self-contained.

records.originalText: Even the smallest child knows that kind a thing.
records.finalText: Even the smallest child knows that kind of thing.
records.rationale: Correct kind a thing to kind of thing; the hyperbolic knowledge statement is ordinary speaker evaluation.

records.originalText: No matter how rich one may be, one cannot live happily without health.
records.finalText: No matter how rich one may be, one cannot live happily without health.
records.rationale: The universal equation of poor health with inability to live happily is unsuitable and unsupported.

records.originalText: What kind of test is that?
records.finalText: What kind of test is that?
records.rationale: The simple test-type question is natural and complete direct speech.

records.originalText: Whatever happens, he won't change his mind.
records.finalText: Whatever happens, he won't change his mind.
records.rationale: Repeats the published prediction that Tom will not change his mind; the concession adds only emphasis.

records.originalText: Come what may, I will not break my word.
records.finalText: Come what may, I will not break my word.
records.rationale: Come what may is a conventional concessive idiom introducing a clear promise.

records.originalText: He isn't going to be forgotten in any case.
records.finalText: He isn't going to be forgotten in any case.
records.rationale: The passive future about a person's memory is grammatical and a situated speaker prediction.

records.originalText: In no case are you to leave your post.
records.finalText: In no case are you to leave your post.
records.rationale: In no case correctly triggers inversion in a direct instruction about remaining at a post.

records.originalText: I would not part with it for the whole world.
records.finalText: I would not part with it for the whole world.
records.rationale: Part with it for the whole world is strongly context-dependent; the valued object is entirely absent.

records.originalText: You must on no condition open the box.
records.finalText: You must on no condition open the box.
records.rationale: On no condition is correctly used in a complete prohibition concerning a specified box.

records.originalText: You should on no condition touch these instruments.
records.finalText: You should on no condition touch these instruments.
records.rationale: Repeats 36803's on-no-condition prohibition with only the target action and object varied.

records.originalText: Whichever you take, you will like it.
records.finalText: Whichever you take, you will like it.
records.rationale: Whichever you take and it lack a supplied choice set or object, leaving a context-only promise.

records.originalText: Choose any one book you like.
records.finalText: Choose any one book you like.
records.rationale: The book-selection instruction is natural and provides an explicit object set.

records.originalText: Take any two cards you like.
records.finalText: Take any two cards you like.
records.rationale: Selecting two cards is a concrete activity with a quantity constraint distinct from the book choice.

records.originalText: Choose three books at random.
records.finalText: Choose three books at random.
records.rationale: At random is a natural manner phrase in a clear three-book instruction.

records.originalText: How long can you hold your breath?
records.finalText: How long can you hold your breath?
records.rationale: The ability question about breath duration is grammatical and gives no hazardous practice instruction.

records.originalText: How long will this cold weather go on?
records.finalText: How long will this cold weather go on?
records.rationale: Go on naturally asks about the continuation of the specified cold weather.

records.originalText: The value of the dollar has fallen recently.
records.finalText: The value of the dollar has fallen recently.
records.rationale: The recent dollar-value claim lacks a date and comparison currency and is not verifiable here.

records.originalText: The exchange rate for the yen against the dollar has risen.
records.finalText: The exchange rate for the yen against the dollar has risen.
records.rationale: The asserted yen-dollar movement lacks a reference period and changes over time.

records.originalText: Do you charge separately for drinks?
records.finalText: Do you charge separately for drinks?
records.rationale: Charge separately for drinks is a natural complete question about service pricing.

records.originalText: Above all things, we must not be selfish.
records.finalText: Above all things, we must not be selfish.
records.rationale: The speaker's moral exhortation uses above all things grammatically and makes no factual policy claim.

records.originalText: Above all, logic requires precise definitions.
records.finalText: Above all, logic requires precise definitions.
records.rationale: Above all presupposes an argument and the claim about what logic requires needs explanatory scope.

records.originalText: Above all, be careful about what you eat and drink.
records.finalText: Above all, be careful about what you eat and drink.
records.rationale: The unqualified dietary caution is context-poor advice and above all refers to an absent priority list.

records.originalText: Will you try to play the trumpet?
records.finalText: Will you try to play the trumpet?
records.rationale: Try to play the trumpet is grammatical, expressing an invitation to attempt the instrument.

records.originalText: What do you say to playing cards?
records.finalText: What do you say to playing cards?
records.rationale: What do you say to plus a gerund is a natural invitation to play cards.

records.originalText: The invention of the transistor marked a new era.
records.finalText: The invention of the transistor marked a new era.
records.rationale: Marked a new era is an unframed historical evaluation whose scope is missing.

records.originalText: Someone stole my traveler's checks.
records.finalText: Someone stole my traveler's checks.
records.rationale: Traveler's checks is a valid American noun phrase in a complete personal theft report.

records.originalText: Which is stronger, a tiger or a lion?
records.finalText: Which is stronger, a tiger or a lion?
records.rationale: The comparative animal question asks an open question without asserting a universal ranking.

records.originalText: The truck made a sharp turn to the right.
records.finalText: The truck made a sharp turn to the right.
records.rationale: Made a sharp turn is a natural movement collocation with a specified direction.

records.originalText: A truck was standing in the middle of the road.
records.finalText: A truck was standing in the middle of the road.
records.rationale: Standing can naturally describe a stationary truck at a specified road location.

records.originalText: What do you say to going for a drive?
records.finalText: What do you say to going for a drive?
records.rationale: Repeats the what-do-you-say-to invitation frame from 36912 with only the leisure activity changed.

records.originalText: Many drivers abandoned their cars in the snow.
records.finalText: Many drivers abandoned their cars in the snow.
records.rationale: Abandoned their cars in the snow describes a specific past transport incident naturally.

records.originalText: In any case, it's wrong to break a promise.
records.finalText: In any case, it's wrong to break a promise.
records.rationale: In any case lacks the preceding argument and the categorical moral maxim adds little independent content.

records.originalText: In any case, I'll have to go there tomorrow.
records.finalText: In any case, I'll have to go there tomorrow.
records.rationale: Have to go there tomorrow is a complete modal plan; in any case is a natural discourse adjunct.

records.originalText: I'm glad to have passed at all.
records.finalText: I'm glad to have passed at all.
records.rationale: Passed at all leaves the examination or qualifying event unidentified and relies on absent contrast.

records.originalText: In any case, it's none of your business.
records.finalText: In any case, it's none of your business.
records.rationale: The dismissive none-of-your-business rejoinder depends entirely on missing prior discourse.

records.originalText: Tom was dismissed without notice.
records.finalText: Tom was dismissed without notice.
records.rationale: Dismissed without notice is a natural passive account of a specific employment event.

records.originalText: Tom awoke to find himself in a strange room.
records.finalText: Tom awoke to find himself in a strange room.
records.rationale: Awoke to find expresses a resulting discovery with a complete strange-room setting.

records.originalText: Tom laid the book aside and looked up.
records.finalText: Tom laid the book aside and looked up.
records.rationale: Laid the book aside and looked up forms a natural pair of past actions.

records.originalText: Tom said he was ill, which was a lie.
records.finalText: Tom said he was ill, which was a lie.
records.rationale: The relative clause clearly evaluates Tom's specific illness statement as untrue.

records.originalText: Tom had no appetite because of his illness.
records.finalText: Tom had no appetite because of his illness.
records.rationale: No appetite because of illness is a bounded personal condition, without a generalized medical claim.

records.originalText: Tom talked too much and let the secret slip.
records.finalText: Tom talked too much and let the secret slip.
records.rationale: Let the secret slip idiomatically describes a particular accidental disclosure.

records.originalText: Tom has grown in strength.
records.finalText: Tom has grown in strength.
records.rationale: Grown in strength is a grammatical, complete description of personal development.

records.originalText: Tom is too honest a boy to tell a lie.
records.finalText: Tom is too honest a boy to tell a lie.
records.rationale: Too honest a boy to tell a lie is a valid adjective-noun infinitive construction in a speaker assessment.

records.originalText: Tom got a grip on his emotions.
records.finalText: Tom got a grip on his emotions.
records.rationale: Got a grip on his emotions is a natural idiom for recovering emotional control.

records.originalText: Tom got so absorbed in his work that he forgot to eat.
records.finalText: Tom got so absorbed in his work that he forgot to eat.
records.rationale: So absorbed that expresses a clear result of engagement in one work episode.

records.originalText: Tom is the last person to break his promise.
records.finalText: Tom is the last person to break his promise.
records.rationale: The last person to break his promise is a natural idiomatic personal assessment.

records.originalText: Tom is by no means unintelligent. He is just lazy.
records.finalText: Tom is by no means unintelligent. He is just lazy.
records.rationale: By no means unintelligent is grammatical litotes followed by a clear contrasting evaluation.

records.originalText: Tom got time and a half when he worked beyond his usual quitting time.
records.finalText: Tom got time and a half when he worked beyond his usual quitting time.
records.rationale: Time and a half and quitting time are valid employment expressions in a particular past event.

records.originalText: Tom showed his courage in the face of danger.
records.finalText: Tom showed his courage in the face of danger.
records.rationale: In the face of danger is a natural phrase describing one person's display of courage.

records.originalText: Tom has a bright career as a medical doctor.
records.finalText: Tom has a bright career ahead of him as a medical doctor.
records.rationale: Has a bright career is awkward for a prediction; ahead of him makes the intended future assessment explicit.

records.originalText: Did Tom use to play hooky?
records.finalText: Did Tom use to play hooky?
records.rationale: Did use to is the correct interrogative form; play hooky is idiomatic American English.

records.originalText: Tom got a small portion of pie.
records.finalText: Tom got a small portion of pie.
records.rationale: A small portion of pie is a natural quantity phrase in a concrete past event.

records.originalText: You can easily identify Tom because he is very tall.
records.finalText: You can easily identify Tom because he is very tall.
records.rationale: The identification explanation uses because naturally and supplies a visible distinguishing feature.

records.originalText: Tom is so intelligent that he stands out in class.
records.finalText: Tom is so intelligent that he stands out in class.
records.rationale: So intelligent that links a subjective assessment and classroom distinction coherently.

records.originalText: Tom happened to let out the secret to his friends.
records.finalText: Tom happened to let out the secret to his friends.
records.rationale: Repeats 37061's accidental disclosure of Tom's secret, adding only the friends as recipients.

records.originalText: Tom may have missed the train. He hasn't come yet.
records.finalText: Tom may have missed the train. He hasn't come yet.
records.rationale: May have missed expresses a plausible past explanation for the stated absence.

records.originalText: Tom got wet to the skin and caught cold.
records.finalText: Tom got wet to the skin and caught cold.
records.rationale: The rain-to-cold causal sequence suggests an unsupported medical inference and repeats the wet-to-the-skin event.

records.originalText: Tom is the most diligent student in class.
records.finalText: Tom is the most diligent student in class.
records.rationale: The classroom superlative is a situated evaluation with a clear comparison group.

records.originalText: No other boy in the class is taller.
records.finalText: No other boy in the class is taller.
records.rationale: Taller has no comparison anchor and no named subject, so the standalone claim is incomplete.

records.originalText: Tom is more hardworking than any other student in his class.
records.finalText: Tom is more hardworking than any other student in his class.
records.rationale: A superlative paraphrase of 37298 with hardworking replacing diligent.

records.originalText: Tom is the most diligent student in his class.
records.finalText: Tom is the most diligent student in his class.
records.rationale: Repeats 37298 almost exactly, differing only in the possessive classroom determiner.

records.originalText: Tom works more diligently now.
records.finalText: Tom works more diligently now.
records.rationale: More diligently now is a natural comparative personal-progress statement with an implicit earlier baseline.

records.originalText: Tom has bought a house which has six rooms.
records.finalText: Tom has bought a house which has six rooms.
records.rationale: Present-perfect purchase plus a relative clause gives a complete specific-house description.

records.originalText: Tom was sitting silent for half an hour.
records.finalText: Tom sat silent for half an hour.
records.rationale: Use sat for the completed half-hour period; the duration and silent behavior remain unchanged.

records.originalText: Tom has a house which has two rooms.
records.finalText: Tom has a house which has two rooms.
records.rationale: Near pragmatic repetition of 37325's house-room description with only the number and possession tense varied.

records.originalText: Tom is the taller of the two boys.
records.finalText: Tom is the taller of the two boys.
records.rationale: The taller of the two boys uses the comparative naturally with an explicit two-person set.

records.originalText: Two high school boys beat Tom black and blue.
records.finalText: Two high school boys beat Tom black and blue.
records.rationale: The graphic assault idiom is unsuitable for the unframed general learner typing lane.

records.originalText: Tom is lying ill in bed.
records.finalText: Tom is lying ill in bed.
records.rationale: Lying ill in bed is grammatical and describes a specific person's state without medical advice.
